candidates.source_name: Profesia.sk — banking/compliance job listings (SK's dominant job board)
candidates.why_relevant: Profesia is the default hiring channel for every SK bank and most PSPs. Job titles and requirement bullets name specific regulations (DORA, PSD2/PSD3, AML/AMLR, CRR3, IFRS, FINREP/COREP, MiCA) months before implementation programmes surface publicly. Employer-filtered views (e.g. company_id) let you track a single bank's regulatory hiring wave over time.
candidates.legal_status: ToS likely restricts scraping; manual/low-rate monitoring and RSS/alerting features preferable
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword+employer saved searches with periodic low-rate polling of listing pages; capture title, employer, salary, and the regulation acronyms in the requirements text
candidates.discovered_via_method: sk-language seed search on job wording
queries_used: pracovná ponuka compliance regulatory reporting banka Bratislava

candidates.source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa careers portal (slsp.topjobs.sk / slsp.sk/kariera)
candidates.why_relevant: Largest SK bank (Erste group). Its own postings carry richer role descriptions than aggregator copies and reveal named programme teams (e.g. regulatory reporting, ICT risk/DORA, AML transformation), which are proxies for internal implementation roadmaps.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the topjobs listing index; diff role titles month over month
queries_used: Slovenská sporiteľňa VÚB ČSOB kariéra "regulatory reporting" specialist job Bratislava profesia

candidates.source_name: Tatra banka careers (prirodzenenajlepsi.sk — Tatra banka / Raiffeisen SK employer site)
candidates.why_relevant: Tatra banka (RBI group) runs its recruitment on a dedicated employer-brand domain rather than the main bank site. Regulatory/compliance vacancies there indicate group-driven implementation programmes landing in SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl vacancy index, filter on compliance/risk/reporting keywords
queries_used: Tatra banka kariéra voľné pracovné miesta compliance regulatory reporting

candidates.source_name: Kariera.sk (Zoznam) — banking compliance vacancies
candidates.why_relevant: Secondary SK job board that carries bank and financial-institution compliance roles not always mirrored on Profesia; useful as a cross-check and for smaller PSPs/e-money firms.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword search pages, low-rate polling

candidates.why_relevant: Aggregator that surfaces postings from employer sites, agencies and niche boards in one place — good for discovering which employers (incl. non-bank PSPs, fintechs, shared-service centres) are hiring regulatory staff, then snowballing to the primary posting.

candidates.source_name: LinkedIn — Slovak bank company job pages (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa)
candidates.why_relevant: SK banks post senior/programme roles (DORA programme manager, regulatory reporting lead, AMLA readiness) in English on LinkedIn that never appear on SK boards. Also surfaces employee title changes that mark a new regulatory function being stood up.

candidates.source_name: ManpowerGroup Slovensko — job postings (agency channel)
candidates.why_relevant: Banks frequently outsource confidential regulatory-programme hiring to agencies; agency ads describe the workstream (e.g. 'reporting to NBS', 'DORA remediation') while masking the client, which is itself a signal that an unannounced programme exists.

candidates.source_name: NBS — Konferencie a podujatia (conferences & events)
candidates.why_relevant: The regulator's own event calendar is a leading indicator: a workshop announced for a regulation signals that supervisory expectations and reporting templates are imminent. Confirmed example found: a DORA workshop on the first level-2 package.

candidates.discovered_via_method: sk-language search + snowball from regulator site

negative_findings.description: No SK-specific job-market analytics product was found that tracks compliance/regulatory hiring volumes over time (Profesia publishes general labour-market reports, but nothing scoped to banking regulation roles).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only raw listing pages and generic aggregators; the time-series signal must be constructed by the collector itself from repeated listing snapshots.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hiring-intensity as a leading indicator only works if snapshots are taken continuously; there is no back-fillable archive, so collection must start now.

negative_findings.description: No SK job posting explicitly naming DORA or PSD3 implementation at a named Slovak bank was retrieved in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: English-language search returned only advisory-firm marketing pages (PwC SK, CyberUpgrade, Validato) and a non-SK GRC job aggregator; the SK boards were not searchable at posting-text level from the search engine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that regulation acronyms in job ads are only reachable by querying the boards' own search (Profesia full-text), not via general web search — this constrains the collection design.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, indexed archive of NBS supervisory officials' speeches other than the governor's page was located (e.g. no separate vice-governor or head-of-supervision speech archive).
negative_findings.result_summary: Vice-governor remarks were found only embedded in individual conference and news pages on nbs.sk.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Supervisory-priority signals from non-governor officials must be harvested from the general Aktuality feed and event pages rather than a clean speech archive.

negative_findings.description: No SK 'compliance officer of the year' / regulatory-practitioner award or professional-body ranking was found; SK awards in scope are product- and bank-level (Zlatá minca, TREND Banka roka).
negative_findings.result_summary: Awards searches in Slovak returned only consumer-product and bank-of-the-year competitions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The awards channel gives actor-mapping value but little direct signal on regulatory implementation programmes; expectations for this sub-channel should be set low.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn — the richest source for English-language senior regulatory-programme roles and for title changes signalling new functions — is login-walled and prohibits scraping.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only company landing pages were reachable without authentication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A whole class of the strongest weak signals is available only via manual analyst review or paid/official access; this is a standing cost, not a fixable bug.

coverage_gaps.description: Career pages of several major SK banks and of non-bank PSPs/e-money institutions were not individually located in this pass — VÚB, ČSOB SK, 365.bank, Prima banka, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK branch, mBank SK, plus payment institutions (e.g. acquirers, PISP/AISP licence holders on the NBS register).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from the NBS register of authorised payment institutions and e-money institutions to build the full employer list, then locate and register each entity's careers URL as its own source.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads and event agendas are ephemeral — postings disappear on close and agenda pages are overwritten for the next edition, so no historical baseline exists.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot listing pages and agendas on a fixed cadence (weekly for jobs, on-publication for agendas) and archive raw HTML; consider Wayback submission for key agenda URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovak job ads at international banking shared-service centres in Bratislava are often written in English, while regulator and training material is Slovak-only; a single-language crawl will systematically miss one half.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run every job and event query in both sk and en, and maintain a bilingual acronym glossary (regulatórny reporting / regulatory reporting; dohľad / supervision; platobné služby / payment services).

coverage_gaps.description: Public-sector and parliamentary speech channels adjacent to NBS were not covered — Ministry of Finance SR officials' conference remarks, and NBS supervisors speaking at third-party events where only the organiser publishes the agenda.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add mfsr.sk speeches/press and cross-reference speaker lists on third-party agendas (Finweek, IBV NBS FinNext, SBA) against NBS/MF SR staff to catch off-site regulator signals.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs (finweek.sk/program, trend.sk award landing, profesia keyword URLs) were derived from search results rather than fetched in this pass, and one is paywalled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pass all URLs to the deterministic liveness verifier; treat 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than dead, and re-resolve any 404 by site search.

brief: For Slovakia's indirect regulatory weak-signal channel, the landscape splits into three usable layers. First, a hiring layer dominated by Profesia.sk plus individual bank career portals (slsp.topjobs.sk, prirodzenenajlepsi.sk for Tatra banka) and agency channels, where regulation acronyms in requirement text are the signal — but this text is only reachable through each board's own full-text search, and nothing is archived, so collection must be snapshot-based and start immediately. Second, an agenda layer that is unusually strong here: NBS runs both its own event calendar (a DORA level-2 workshop page was found) and the IBV NBS training institute it founded, whose ~120-course catalogue and FinNext AML & Compliance conference are demand-driven and therefore lead formal disclosure; Finweek Bratislava, SBA and the Slovak Fintech Association supply the industry-side agendas. Third, a speech and awards layer centred on the NBS governor's interviews-and-presentations archive and the Aktuality feed, with Zlatá minca and TREND Banka roka useful mainly for actor mapping rather than regulatory timing. The main structural weaknesses are LinkedIn's login wall over the richest senior-role signals, the absence of career-page coverage for VÚB, ČSOB, 365.bank and licensed non-bank PSPs, and the lack of any speech archive for NBS officials below the governor.
